lead.headline: Houthis take Mocha and a strait island, closing their grip on Bab al-Mandeb
lead.dek: Boats carrying fighters reached Mayyun Island on Friday; the U.N. envoy warns of full-scale war and Brent holds above $100
body: Yemen's Houthi rebels seized the Red Sea port city of Mocha on Thursday after government forces withdrew, Yemeni officials and Houthi media said, giving the Iran-backed group control of nearly all of Yemen's Red Sea coast and a position about 80 kilometers (50 miles) from the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

Tariq Saleh of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council called the retreat a "tactical withdrawal" to regroup. France 24 reported the coastal fighting since last week has killed more than 500 people, most of them combatants, and displaced nearly 20,000. The Houthi-run Saba agency said Saudi jets flew 40 more strikes Thursday on Taiz, Hodeidah, al-Jawf and Marib.

By Friday morning boats carrying Houthi fighters had reached Mayyun Island, in the middle of the strait, after government forces withdrew, a local official told AFP. The U.N. Security Council met in emergency session Thursday; envoy Hans Grundberg said Yemen faces its gravest risk of full-scale war since the 2022 truce, and crude is trading above $100 a barrel.

art.caption: A loading-dock doorway above standing floodwater in Point Pleasant on Thursday, the door and a utility pole reflected in the still water.

briefs.headline: Vance and Trump close the GOP's midterm convention in Dallas
briefs.summary: Vance told voters who differ with Republicans on an issue to "vote for us anyway" and skipped the $5,000 dividend; Trump repeated it and told the hall to "pretend that I'm running." Gov. Ron DeSantis of Florida said it would add debt.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court rejects Missouri's Trump-backed map; 2022 lines return
briefs.summary: The court on Thursday, with no noted dissents, refused to let Missouri use districts drawn last year; Secretary of State Denny Hoskins then sent counties back to the 2022 map under a contempt threat. Over a million voters get new candidates, AP estimated.

briefs.headline: Wholesale prices rose 0.4% in August as diesel jumped 24.1%
briefs.summary: The final-demand index is up 5.4% over 12 months, BLS said Thursday; goods rose 1.1% on a 4.2% energy gain, services 0.1%. Core prices less food, energy and trade rose 0.3% for the month and 4.7% for the year. CPI follows at 8:30 a.m.

briefs.headline: CBS: an A-10 lost a wing, eight F-15s hit in Iran's strike on Jordan base
briefs.summary: People with direct knowledge told CBS News the A-10 was struck and about eight F-15s took light damage and returned to service in Tuesday night's attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base; no U.S. deaths were reported. Over 30 Patriots were fired.

briefs.headline: Russian strike on a Pavlohrad mall kills 5, injures 67
briefs.summary: The midday strike Thursday on a shopping center in the Dnipropetrovsk Oblast city, 75 kilometers from the front, killed five and injured at least 67, authorities said; three boys aged 13 to 15 were among the hurt. Video suggests a drone hit after the first blast.

briefs.headline: School fire in rebel-held Bukavu kills at least 29
briefs.summary: A fire and stampede at two schools in the eastern Congo city killed at least 29 people Thursday, local officials said; M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka said the dead included 19 girls and five boys. About 300 homes burned; the cause is not established.

briefs.headline: Hong Kong jails three Tiananmen vigil organizers for up to 7 years
briefs.summary: A national security court sentenced Chow Hang-tung to seven years and three months, Lee Cheuk-yan to seven years and Albert Ho, who pleaded guilty, to five years and two months for inciting subversion. Lee and Chow plan to appeal, relatives said.

briefs.headline: Spanish lawmakers back citizenship for Sahrawis born under Spanish rule
briefs.summary: The lower house voted 168-31 Thursday for a bill granting Spanish nationality to Western Saharans born before Sept. 29, 1977, and their descendants; about 80,000 are believed eligible. The People's Party abstained and the Senate must still approve it.

briefs.headline: Point Pleasant floods after 6 to 8 inches of rain; Mason schools close
briefs.summary: Storm Team 8 estimated 6 to 8 inches fell on Point Pleasant on Thursday, closing Mason County Schools and the Piggly Wiggly and putting Jericho and Jones roads under water; WSAZ listed eight county roads closed by 8 a.m.

briefs.headline: Armstrong to run 500 miles of fiber to 5,000 homes in 10 counties
briefs.summary: Gov. Morrisey, Sen. Capito and FCC Commissioner Olivia Trusty announced the $100M public-private buildout Thursday; state LEAD projects are largely done, E-ACAM work is under way and BEAD groundbreaking comes next.

briefs.headline: Logan Elementary will not reopen; district to renovate the middle school
briefs.summary: Seven months after the February fire, Logan County Schools said Thursday the 60-year-old building is not feasible to repair; Superintendent Sonya White told MetroNews she will ask the School Building Authority in November to fund a combined school at Logan Middle.

briefs.headline: Charter board eyes tuition for out-of-state students in border counties
briefs.summary: At Thursday's virtual meeting Executive Director Barry Holstein said he wants code changed so border-county charters can enroll and bill out-of-state students as county systems do; House Education Chairman Joe Statler questioned relying on that tuition.

regional.item: Huntington's planning commission approved HADCO's site plan for a 40,000-square-foot spec industrial building at 7th Avenue and 29th Street.
Kanawha County Schools held its first excess-levy town hall in Nitro on Wednesday ahead of the November renewal vote, with more meetings to come.
Wood County commissioners want to meet Peoples Cartage leaders over an unanswered $289,000 SPSI bill for pumping river water at July's warehouse fire.
The 56th Nicholas County Potato Festival opens today in downtown Summersville and runs through Saturday with a parade, 5K and fireworks.

away.item: The SVUESD board on Tuesday named chair Sandy Foster its representative to the Act 170 school-merger study group, which must meet before Oct. 15.

hotspots.item: Smoke traced to a motor briefly emptied the Webster County Courthouse with no structure fire, Fire Chief Don McCourt said, the Webster Echo reported Tuesday.
North Topsail Beach Fire and Rescue holds a 110-floor 9/11 memorial stair climb Friday at 8:46 a.m. at the St. Regis Resort, open to the public.

briefs.headline: Council lets Croft Road house proceed after city permit error
briefs.summary: Council voted Monday to let a house at 2239 Croft Road keep a foundation 1.17 metres from the rear line, not the six metres zoning requires, after a 2023 city permit error. Mayor Simon Yu and councillors Kyle Sampson and Brian Skakun voted no.

briefs.headline: Elev8 names six incumbents it will campaign against
briefs.summary: The group led by Jason Luke dropped plans to endorse eight candidates and will buy ads on the records of mayoral candidate Kyle Sampson and councillors Garth Frizzell, Cori Ramsay, Ron Polillo, Tim Bennett and Susan Scott.

briefs.headline: Nisga'a and Tahltan open majority Indigenous-owned port at Stewart
briefs.summary: The Portland Canal Marine Terminal, 310 kilometres northwest of Terrace, marked its official opening this week; it ships about 300,000 tonnes of copper and gold concentrate a year. The province put $5 million toward the purchase.

briefs.headline: Surrey starts demolition for a 10,000-seat arena
briefs.summary: Mayor Brenda Locke began tearing down a former downtown Safeway on Thursday for an arena with a net cost of $360 million, due to open in 2030 with the WHL's Vancouver Giants as anchor tenant. The Imagine Surrey party called it 'a deal done in the dark.'

briefs.headline: Carney and Zelenskyy sign 100-year pact built on drones
briefs.summary: The declaration signed in Calgary on Thursday spans defence, trade, energy and critical minerals. Carney said Canada will build capacity to make millions of drones within two years; the military now holds 2,000.

briefs.headline: Carney says Ottawa won't fund federalist side in Alberta vote
briefs.summary: Asked twice at the Banff cabinet retreat Thursday whether Ottawa would pay for get-out-the-vote work before the Oct. 19 separation referendum, Carney said the system 'is not a money game.' Vote to Stay had raised $97,791 by Sept. 3.

briefs.headline: SpaceX launches classified USSF-153 payload from Vandenberg
briefs.summary: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4E at 11:42 a.m. ET Thursday with an undisclosed number of Space Force satellites bound for low Earth orbit. Booster B1081 landed on a drone ship after its 27th flight; Space Systems Command said mission details are protected.

briefs.headline: Chemotherapy shifts which mutant cells win in healthy gullet tissue
briefs.summary: Sequencing 324 cancer genes in normal oesophageal tissue from 70 patients, a Wellcome Sanger Institute team found chemoradiotherapy enriched cells with TP53 and PPM1D mutations, and chemotherapy alone favored cells resistant to 5-fluorouracil. The paper is in Nature Genetics.

briefs.headline: Mercury has shrunk 10% to 30% more than estimated, DLR team finds
briefs.summary: Impact debris on Mercury's roughest terrain hides contraction scarps, a German Aerospace Center team reported Thursday in Geophysical Research Letters. The correction puts the planet's lost diameter at up to 23 km, against the 4 km to 16 km previously estimated.

briefs.headline: Heat, pollution raise frailty and PTSD risk in 9/11 responders
briefs.summary: A Mount Sinai study of 18,734 World Trade Center responders in New York City, published Friday in Nature Communications, found those in hotter, more polluted neighborhoods had higher risks of frailty, PTSD and depression; greener surroundings tracked with lower risk of all three.

briefs.headline: Anthropic says Alibaba ran 151M-exchange campaign to copy Claude
briefs.summary: Anthropic's threat report Thursday said operators it attributes to Alibaba's Qwen lab pulled 151 million exchanges from Claude between May and July via 3,500-plus fake accounts, and that Moonshot and DeepSeek routed customers' requests to Claude to harvest training data. The figures are Anthropic's own.

briefs.headline: AI agents breached 395 organizations through PaperCut flaws
briefs.summary: GreyNoise traced a campaign that used hundreds of autonomous agents, run on OpenAI's Codex harness and a DeepSeek model, to exploit two PaperCut print-server bugs at 440-plus instances in 48 countries, 204 of them schools. Some agents hit countries the operator excluded.

briefs.headline: Study counts 84 cases of AI-generated filings swamping agencies
briefs.summary: A paper by Chris Schmitz with the Cooperative AI Foundation and GovAI found AI-written filings surging at public bodies in 11 jurisdictions, TechCrunch reported; U.K. housing ombudsman complaints rose from 2,600 in 2022 to 7,000 in 2025. Most filers were entitled to what they claimed, Schmitz said.

kicker: Summers County ran no regional line; August CPI comes at 8:30 a.m., after this edition, and the Topsail Beach hens vote still has no posted result.
